findings.evidence: description names .com, .io, .app, .dev and RDAP/WHOIS, but not the WHOIS-only TLDs the body treats specially (.co, .de, .es, .mx)
findings.fix: Brainstorm, screen and rank brandable domain names (.com, .io, .app, .dev, and WHOIS-only TLDs such as .co) for apps, products, companies and personal brands, and report registration status honestly via RDAP/WHOIS lookups. Use when naming a project, launching or rebranding, asking "is this domain available", or replacing a taken first choice, even if the user only describes the business. Not for DNS, email, hosting or transfers on a domain already owned, naming without domains, social handles, or legal trademark clearance.

findings.evidence: Step 4.2 packs five things into one bullet: the score formula, the unknown-reach rule, the unscored fallback, the strategic-bet override and the pointer to the Frequency and Defensibility lenses.

findings.fix: Add one sentence after the formula: the score orders ideas within a tier but does not decide for you. When the formula's order goes against the cited evidence, keep the evidence-led order and write the reason in the Deciding trade-off cell.
